title: What pytest actually collects
brief: "It says 0 tests collected" is the single most common first-day problem, and it is almost always a naming rule. Three questions.

questions.prompt: A file called `login_test.py` contains `def test_login(page): ...`. You run `pytest`. What happens?
options: It runs - the function is named test_login
It is ignored - the FILE must start with test_ too
It runs, but only with the --strict flag
It errors, because a test file cannot end in _test.py
questions.why: Both halves of the rule must hold: the file must match test_*.py AND the function must start with test_. Rename it to test_login.py and it is collected. (pytest can be configured to accept *_test.py as well, but the kit's pytest.ini does not - stick to the default and you will never be surprised.)

questions.prompt: Inside `test_cart.py` you write `def check_cart_total(page): ...`. Does pytest run it?
options: Yes - it is in a test file
No - the function name does not start with test_
Only if another test calls it
Only if it contains an assert
questions.why: pytest collects by NAME, not by content. check_cart_total is just a function sitting in a file that nobody calls. This is genuinely useful: helper functions live safely next to tests precisely because they are not named test_.

questions.prompt: Where does the `page` argument come from in `def test_home(page):`?
options: You have to create it: page = Browser().new_page()
It is a pytest fixture from the pytest-playwright plugin - a fresh tab per test
It is a global variable pytest sets before the run
It is optional and always None unless you pass it yourself
questions.why: pytest matches the argument name to a registered fixture. pytest-playwright provides `page` and hands each test a brand-new browser tab, which is why tests cannot leak state into each other through the browser. The kit's conftest.py says exactly this in its opening comment.

reveal: Naming is discovery. If a test is not running, read its file name and its function name before you read anything else.
